SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfill all eligibility conditions as on the date of eligibility (01-04-2026). Only Indian Citizens are eligible to apply. Candidates must mandatorily register on the NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) before applying online. Candidates can apply for engagement in one State only and can appear for the examination only once under this engagement project.

Criteria Details
Registration Requirement Mandatory registration on NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) before applying online through SBI website (https://www.sbi.co.in/careers or https://sbi.bank.in/careers).
Educational Qualification (as on 01-04-2026) Graduation from a recognized University / Institute.
Prior Apprenticeship Candidate should NOT have undergone Apprenticeship either in SBI or in any other organization earlier, and should not currently be pursuing Apprenticeship Training as per the Apprentices Act 1961 as amended.
Training / Job Experience Candidates who had training or job experience for a period of 1 year or more after attainment of educational qualification shall NOT be eligible.
CIBIL Candidates who have defaulted in repayment under any lending arrangement with Banks/NBFCs/Financial Institutions including credit card dues and have not regularized/repaid outstanding till date of issuance of offer of engagement shall not be eligible.
Aadhaar Requirement All candidates (except those belonging to Northeastern States where alternate ID proof will do) should produce Aadhaar Number before engagement, i.e., contract signing for apprenticeship training.
Nationality Indian Citizens only.

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Age Limit

Candidates must be a minimum of 20 years and maximum of 28 years as on 01-04-2026, i.e., candidates must have been born not later than 01-04-2006 and not earlier than 02-04-1998 (both days inclusive). Maximum age indicated is for Unreserved and EWS candidates. Relaxation in upper age limit is applicable as per Government of India guidelines for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates.

PwBD As per Government of India guidelines

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Application Fee

Candidates are required to pay non-refundable Fees/Intimation Charges through online mode only. The process of registration is complete only when fee is deposited with the Bank through online mode on or before the last date for payment of fees. Fee once paid will NOT be refunded on any account nor can it be held in reserve for any other exam or selection.

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection for engagement of apprentices will be based on (i) Online Written Test and (ii) Test of Local Language, followed by Medical Examination. Final selection is subject to verification of eligibility, qualifying in local language test, and medical fitness. A Wait List (State-category wise) will be maintained for one year from the date of result or next engagement exercise, whichever is earlier. Candidates will be released only once from this waitlist against non-joining subject to availability of qualified candidates.

Each test has a separate timing as mentioned above. There will be NEGATIVE MARKS for wrong answers — 1/4th of the mark assigned for the question will be deducted for each wrong answer. Test questions (except General English) will be set in 13 Regional Languages viz. Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu — in addition to English and Hindi — as applicable State-wise. SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates get 5% relaxation in minimum qualifying marks on aggregate. Merit list will be drawn State-wise and Category-wise in descending order; tie-break is by age in descending order.

Stage 2 - Test of Local Language

The test of specified local language will be conducted after qualifying the online written examination. Candidates who fail to qualify this test will not be engaged as apprentice. Candidates who produce 10th or 12th standard mark sheet/certificate evidencing having studied the specified local language will not be required to undergo the language test. Candidates must appear at their own expense; SBI will not reimburse travelling expenses.

Stage 3 - Medical Examination

Engagement of selected apprentices is subject to being declared medically fit as per the requirement of the Bank and satisfactory completion of KYE formalities.

SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 - Weightage in Junior Associate Recruitment

Weightage/Relaxation to apprentices in recruitment of Junior Associates shall be given as per the recruitment policy of the Bank as amended from time to time, to apprentices who successfully complete the apprenticeship training in SBI, subject to candidate's satisfactory conduct and performance during the entire training period. Successful completion refers to passing of the skill evaluation test (Trade test) and obtention of the joint National Apprenticeship Certificate issued by SBI-NSDC / BFSI-SSC.

Competition Level Analysis for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026

The competition level for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very high due to 7150 seats being offered at the all-India level and the exam being open to any graduate, including those already preparing for bank and SSC exams. While the written test is of easy to moderate difficulty and slightly below SBI Clerk level, the large number of serious aspirants in high-population states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana will push state-wise and category-wise cut-offs upward.

In practical terms, each seat is likely to attract dozens to over a hundred candidates in major states, making speed, accuracy, and sectional balance crucial to clearing the single-stage written exam followed by the local language test. However, the effective competition reduces at later stages because some candidates will fail to qualify the language test or be filtered out at the document verification, CIBIL, Aadhaar, and medical fitness stages, and SBI will finally select candidates strictly on state-wise and category-wise merit from those who clear all stages.

Who should NOT apply for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates looking for a permanent job in SBI; this is only a 1‑year apprenticeship with no guarantee of absorption or regular employment.
  • Candidates who already completed any Apprenticeship (in SBI or any other organisation) or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training under the Apprentices Act.
  • Candidates outside the age band 20–28 years as on the cut-off date (even 1 day younger/older is not eligible, except notified relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD).
  • Aspirants who do not have a Graduation degree from a recognised University/Institute by the specified date.
  • Candidates not fluent in the notified local language of the State/UT (reading, writing, speaking, understanding), and who are unlikely to clear the language test or do not have 10th/12th proof.
  • Candidates unwilling or unable to register on the NAPS portal before applying, as this is a mandatory prerequisite for SBI Apprentice.
  • Candidates with serious CIBIL/loan/credit‑card defaults who have not regularised or repaid outstanding dues by the time of offer; such profiles are normally rejected in bank recruitments.
  • Ex‑Servicemen / Disabled Ex‑Servicemen, where the notification clearly states no engagement / no reservation for them under Apprentice.
  • PwBD candidates whose disability type falls under “likely to improve” (temporary disability) where reservation benefits may not apply as per notification conditions.
  • Candidates who cannot produce valid Aadhaar (except where exempted, e.g., certain North‑Eastern states with alternate ID allowed).

Common mistakes / What to check before applying SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

  • Applying in a wrong State or language where you cannot comfortably read, write and speak the specified local language.
  • Entering wrong category (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/UR); category cannot be changed later and mismatch with certificates at DV can lead to cancellation.
  • OBC candidates from creamy layer applying as OBC instead of UR; only non‑creamy OBCs with valid, recent certificate get reservation.
  • Uploading blurred/incorrect photo, signature, thumb impression or declaration (wrong size, wrong format, someone else’s handwriting) leading to rejection at scrutiny.
  • Using invalid or inactive mobile number/email ID, causing failure to receive OTPs, registration details, call letters or further communication.
  • Submitting multiple applications for different states or with different details; SBI usually accepts only the last complete application and may forfeit extra fees.
  • Ignoring negative marking and over‑attempting in the exam, which can sharply reduce your score despite high attempts.
  • Not reading the clause that this is not regular employment, and later protesting about absorption or permanent posting after apprenticeship ends.

How to Apply for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online; no other mode of application will be accepted. Candidates must first mandatorily register on the NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) and read the detailed guidelines on https://bfsissc.com before applying online through the SBI website.

Candidates should have a valid email ID and mobile number which should be kept active till declaration of results. Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date and not wait till the last date.

Documents Required to be Scanned and Uploaded (as per Annexure-I):

  • Recent passport-size colour photograph (4.5 cm × 3.5 cm; 200×230 pixels; 20 KB–50 KB; JPEG)
  • Signature with black ink on white paper (140×60 pixels; 10 KB–20 KB; JPEG)
  • Left Thumb Impression on white paper with black or blue ink (240×240 pixels; 20 KB–50 KB; JPEG/JPG)
  • Handwritten Declaration in English on white paper with black ink (800×400 pixels; 50 KB–100 KB; JPEG/JPG) — in candidate's own handwriting
  • Live photograph captured via webcam or mobile phone (to be uploaded at the time of online application)

Documents to be Produced at the time of Examination / Document Verification / Engagement:

  • Call Letter (downloaded from Bank's website) along with photo identity proof (Passport / Aadhaar / PAN Card / Driving License / Voter's Card / Bank Passbook with photograph / Identity Card issued by School or College / Gazetted Officer in official letterhead) in original and self-attested photocopy
  • Caste Certificate in prescribed Government of India format (for SC/ST candidates) — to be submitted at the time of engagement if called for
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed Government of India format, issued during the period 01-04-2026 to the date of joining (for OBC candidates)
  • Income and Asset Certificate issued by Competent Authority in the format prescribed by Government of India, valid for the year 2026-27 (for EWS candidates)
  • Disability Certificate in prescribed format issued by a Competent Authority as per Government of India guidelines (for PwBD candidates)
  • Educational qualification certificates and marksheets (Graduation onwards)

Printout of Application Form is NOT to be sent to SBI. No Hard Copy of the Call Letter for Online Written Examination will be sent by post. Candidates must appear for the test at their own cost; SBI will not pay or reimburse any such expenses.

Apply Online at: https://www.sbi.co.in/careers or https://sbi.bank.in/careers

For queries: Call 022-22820427 (11:00 AM to 06:00 PM on working days) or visit https://cgrs.ibps.in — mention "Engagement of Apprentice in SBI" in the subject.

Important Instructions for SBI Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • THIS IS NOT AN EMPLOYMENT IN THE BANK. NOR IS THE SAME CONTRACT EMPLOYMENT. Candidates engaged as Apprentice will NOT be treated as "employees" of SBI and will not be entitled to receive any benefits available for employees of the Bank.
  • SBI shall have no obligation to offer regular employment to Apprentices during and/or after the completion of the Apprenticeship period. After completion, candidates will be relieved from the respective work area.
  • Candidates can apply for engagement in one State only and can appear for the examination only once under this engagement project.
  • Mandatory registration on NAPS portal (https://apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) before applying online on SBI website is required.
  • No Ex-Servicemen / Disabled Ex-Servicemen shall be engaged as an Apprentice and there is no reservation for Ex-Servicemen in the Apprentice Engagement.
  • OBC candidates belonging to the "Creamy Layer" are not entitled to reservation/relaxation; they should apply as General or General (LD/VI/HI/d&e) as applicable.
  • Change of category will not be permitted after registration of online application.
  • Candidates with CIBIL default record (unpaid loans/credit card dues) are not eligible for engagement until dues are regularized/repaid.
  • All candidates (except Northeastern State candidates) must produce Aadhaar Number before engagement/contract signing.
  • Not more than one application should be submitted; in case of multiple applications, only the last valid completed application will be retained and fee paid for other registrations will stand forfeited.
  • PwBD candidates with disability conditions falling under "likely to improve" (temporary disability) category are not eligible for reservation.
  • PwBD candidates eligible for scribe facility: candidates with 40% or more disability having physical limitation to write are eligible. Scribe must be arranged by the candidate at his/her own cost. Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination is allowed (whether availing scribe or not) for eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Candidates are advised to keep their registered email ID/mobile active for receiving call letters/advices etc.
  • Mobile phones, smartwatches, pagers, earphones or any other electronic/communication devices are not allowed inside the examination premises.
  • All revisions/corrigendum (if any) will be hosted on the Bank's website only — candidates should visit regularly.
  • No request for change of examination centre shall be entertained. No Travel Expenses will be reimbursed/paid by SBI.
  • Canvassing in any form will be a disqualification.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this recruitment shall be Mumbai only.
  • Bank reserves right to cancel the selection process partly/entirely at any stage.

RRB Technician Vacancy 2026 – Post Details

  • Technician Grade I Signal – 323 Posts
  • Technician Grade III – 6,242 Posts

Who Can Apply for RRB Technician 2026?

Eligibility criteria depend on the post and level. Candidates must meet educational, technical, and age requirements as per the Centralised Employment Notification.

  • Technician Grade I Signal: B.Sc. (Physics / Electronics / Computer Science / IT / Instrumentation) or Degree/Diploma in Engineering in relevant discipline from a recognized institution.
  • Technician Grade III: 10th / Matriculation plus ITI from NCVT/SCVT in relevant trade or Act Apprenticeship in the concerned trade.
  • Other Conditions: Candidates must satisfy prescribed medical standards and citizenship norms and should be within the specified age limit as on the date mentioned in CEN 02/2026.

Age Limit

  • Technician Grade I Signal: 18 to 36 Years
  • Technician Grade III: 18 to 33 Years
  • Upper age relaxation for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/NCL/EWS/Ex-Servicemen/ PWBD) will be applicable as per Government of India rules and details will be given in the detailed CEN. 

Selection Process

RRB Technician recruitment involves multiple stages including a Computer Based Test and subsequent document and medical verification. There is no Computer Based Aptitude Test for these Technician posts.

  • Stage 1: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Stage 2: Document Verification
  • Stage 3: Medical Examination

RRB Technician Exam Pattern 2026

  • Mode of Exam: Computer Based Test (CBT)
  • Total Questions: 100 Objective Type Questions
  • Total Marks: 100 Marks
  • Exam Duration: 90 Minutes
  • Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark will be deducted for each wrong answer; no negative marks for unattempted questions. 

Salary Details

  • Technician Grade I Signal: Pay Level 5 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 29,200/-
  • Technician Grade III: Pay Level 2 (7th CPC) – Initial Pay Rs. 19,900/-
  • Additional allowances such as DA, HRA, TA and other benefits will be admissible as per Railway rules for the respective pay levels. 

How to Apply for RRB Technician Recruitment 2026

  • Visit your regional RRB website (e.g., Ahmedabad, Ajmer, Bengaluru, Chennai, Secunderabad, etc.).
  • Open the link for Centralised Employment Notification CEN 02/2026 – Technician.
  • Read the detailed notification carefully including post-wise eligibility, instructions and list of RRBs.
  • Register by providing basic details like name, mobile number and email ID.
  • Login using the registration credentials and fill the online application form for the desired post and pay level (only one RRB and one pay level allowed per candidate).
  • Upload required documents, photograph and signature as per specifications. >Pay the prescribed application fee through online mode, if applicable.
  • Submit the application form and take a printout / save PDF for future reference.

Important Points Mentioned in Indicative Notice

  • Each candidate can apply to only one RRB for a specific pay level and only one common online application is allowed for all notified posts in that pay level.
  • Separate applications must be submitted for each pay level, if eligible.
  • Candidates are strongly advised to verify name, date of birth and other details using Aadhaar to avoid mismatches at later stages.
  • RRBs caution candidates to be aware of touts, brokers and job racketeers and to rely only on official RRB websites for genuine information.

SSC CGL 2026 – Selection Process

Selection is through a two-tier Computer Based Examination (CBE). Marks scored in CBE conducted in multiple shifts will be normalized as per the procedure published by SSC vide Notice dated 02-06-2025. There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores at any stage.

Tier-I consists of Objective Type / MCQ questions, set in English and Hindi (except English Comprehension). Negative marking: 0.50 marks per wrong answer.

Tier-II: Computer Based Examination

Tier-II is conducted in Paper-I, Paper-II, and Paper-III in separate shifts/days.

Negative marking in Tier-II: 1 mark per wrong answer in Section-I, II, III of Paper-I; 0.50 marks in Paper-II and Paper-III. Section-III (CKT) and Section-IV (DEST) are qualifying in nature. Candidates must qualify all sections of Paper-I separately. Higher standards of CKT and DEST are set for specific posts (CSS, MEA, AFHQ, SFIO, CBIC, Postal etc.). Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe.

SSC CGL 2026 – Exam Centres

The examination will be conducted through 9 SSC Regions covering all states and union territories. Candidates must choose three examination centres, in order of priority, within the same region.

No request for change of centre will be entertained after submission of the application. SSC may add, cancel, or shift candidates to another centre depending on administrative requirements.

Competition Level Analysis for SSC CGL 2026

The overall competition level for SSC CGL 2026 is expected to remain very high because the examination attracts a massive number of graduate applicants every year across India. Even with around 12,256 vacancies, the effective competition ratio remains extremely tough for high-demand posts.

  1. Applicant volume is huge: SSC CGL is among the most sought-after central government exams, and premium posts receive intense preference from top scorers.
  2. Tier-I acts as the main screening stage: With negative marking and sectional timing, both speed and accuracy matter. Candidates targeting top posts generally need a very strong Tier-I score.
  3. Tier-II gets post-specific: Specialized posts like JSO and AAO attract a smaller but more qualified pool, making domain preparation more important than raw competition numbers.
  4. DEST and CKT can eliminate candidates: Although qualifying in nature, poor performance in these sections can disqualify otherwise strong candidates for certain posts.
  5. Physical standards create an extra filter: Certain Inspector and Sub Inspector posts require physical and medical fitness standards that are checked separately by user departments.

Who Should NOT Apply for SSC CGL 2026?

  1. Candidates who will not possess a Bachelor's Degree by 01-08-2026.
  2. Candidates who fall outside the age limit for all eligible posts even after applicable relaxation.
  3. OBC Creamy Layer candidates intending to claim OBC reservation.
  4. Candidates who cannot meet post-specific physical or medical standards for the posts they plan to prefer.
  5. Non-matriculate Ex-Servicemen or those who have not completed the required length of service.
  6. Candidates applying for JSO without the required Mathematics or Statistics qualification.
  7. Female candidates applying specifically for BRO vacancies, where only male candidates are eligible.
  8. Distance-learning degree holders without valid UGC-DEB approval for the relevant period.

Common Mistakes / What to Check Before Applying SSC CGL 2026

  1. Not generating a fresh OTR on the new SSC website.
  2. Using a pre-existing photograph instead of live photo capture where required.
  3. Uploading blurred or wrongly sized signature files.
  4. Selecting the wrong reservation category without valid supporting certificate.
  5. Ignoring post-specific standards before locking post preferences.
  6. Choosing JSO or AAO related preferences without being ready for Paper-II or Paper-III.
  7. Skipping Aadhaar-based authentication even when eligible.
  8. Waiting until the final date for application submission.
  9. Missing the answer key objection window after examination.
  10. Confusing the correction window fee structure.

How to Apply for SSC CGL 2026

Candidates must apply online only at https://ssc.gov.in or through the mY SSC mobile application (available on Store). No other mode of application is accepted. Candidates who have not generated OTR on the new website must do so first. Once OTR is generated on the new website, it remains valid for all future examinations on that portal.

Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-based authentication during OTR. Aadhaar-authenticated candidates get significant exemptions: their applications are not rejected for photograph/signature standards, and they need not carry photo ID at the examination venue.

Steps to Apply:

  1. Generate One-Time Registration (OTR) at https://ssc.gov.in (mandatory; use Aadhaar-based authentication if possible)
  2. Complete OTR profile and lock it
  3. Fill the Common Application Form (CAF) including live photograph capture via camera
  4. Upload scanned signature (JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm)
  5. Fill the Examination Specific Module (post preferences, exam centre choices - 3 centres within same region in order of priority)
  6. Pay application fee of Rs. 100/- online (if applicable) by 23-06-2026
  7. Preview/Print the application to verify all details before final submission
  8. Use the correction window (29-06 to 01-07-2026) if any correction is needed (chargeable)
  9. Keep printout of application and all documents for at least 3 years

Documents to Keep Ready for Document Verification (after final selection):

  • Matriculation/Secondary School Certificate (proof of date of birth)
  • Mark sheets for all years/semesters of Graduation + Provisional/Degree Certificate
  • SC/ST Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure of the notification)
  • OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) Certificate in prescribed format (Annexure-X); must be valid as on closing date of application
  • EWS Income & Asset Certificate valid for FY 2026–27 (issued based on income for FY 2025–26) in prescribed format (Annexure-XI)
  • PwBD Disability Certificate from competent authority specifying type of disability (as per Annexure-XII to XIII)
  • Ex-Serviceman discharge certificate and other relevant ESM documents
  • Equivalence certificate (for equivalent qualifications other than standard degrees)
  • DEB/UGC approval letter (for Distance Learning degree holders)
  • Certificate of proficiency in State Regional/official language (for AAO/Assistant Audit Officer State Cadre)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in | Toll Free Helpline: 1800 309 3063

Important Instructions for SSC CGL 2026 Candidates

  • Final allotment is based on merit-cum-preference, and no alternate post will be offered if a candidate fails post-specific standards after allotment.
  • OBC candidates claiming reservation must not belong to the creamy layer as on the closing date of application.
  • EWS certificate must be valid for FY 2026–27 and should be based on income for FY 2025–26.
  • PwBD candidates must choose the correct sub-category in the application form because no later change is allowed.
  • Scribe rules are strict: the scribe must complete OTR, be Aadhaar-authenticated, and cannot assist more than one candidate.
  • Compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour is available to eligible PwBD candidates.
  • Tentative answer keys can be challenged online by paying Rs. 100 per question within the specified period only.
  • No re-evaluation or re-checking of scores is available at any stage.
  • Candidates should preserve the application form and related documents for at least 3 years.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the Appointing Authority.
  • Fraudulent claims of reservation status may lead to debarment from all SSC examinations.
  • Any update in exam schedule or process will be communicated through the SSC website only.
  • Applications without the required fee, unless exempted, or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 – Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfill all eligibility conditions as on the last date of application. Only Indian citizens are eligible. Candidates must mandatorily possess the Kannada language proficiency as specified. Eligibility details are as follows:

Criteria Details
Educational Qualification PUC (Pre-University Certificate) or equivalent qualification (as on last date of application). Candidates appearing in PUC exam and awaiting results are NOT eligible. All subjects and marks must have been secured by the last date.
PUC Equivalents Accepted (i) Class 12 exam by CBSE or ICSE boards; (ii) Class 12 exam by other state government exam boards; (iii) Higher Secondary education course (HSC) by NIOS (National Institute of Open Schooling); (iv) Two-year BTEC course by NIOS - candidates who passed one language paper and one academic subject in distance/correspondence mode, or appeared in pre-university exam - only in one language and one subject with pass marks, are treated as equivalent to PUC
Vocational courses (GTC) As per Govt. Order No. ED 19 TVE 2019 dated 06.08.2021 - Karnataka State Vocational Training courses (GTC) are treated as equivalent to PUC only for: (i) Compassionate appointment and those already in service under the order; (ii) GTC/PUC marks considered as minimum academic qualification for competitive exams only - GTC is the minimum academic qualification
3-Year Diploma As per Govt. Order No. ED 33 TVE 2021 dated 30.09.2021 - 3-year diploma holders treated as PUC equivalent only for: (i) Direct/compassionate appointment and higher education in technical education department; (ii) Diploma passed before 2015 from a govt. technical institution must pass Kannada language test conducted by KPSC along with the department exam

Candidates who have previously passed the Karnataka Rajyotsava Kannada exam are exempted from this requirement.

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 – Age Limit

Minimum age: 18 years. Maximum age (for direct/unreserved candidates): 33 years as on the last date of application. Age relaxation is available as per Karnataka Government norms. A one-time relaxation of 5 years in upper age limit is available for candidates who have been unjustly denied age relaxation as per Govt. Order No. GAD 262 SEN 2025 dated 29.01.2026.

Category (Direct / Male, Female & Third Gender) Maximum Age
General Merit (UR) 33 years
SC / ST / Category-1 / Cat-2A / Cat-2B / Cat-3A / Cat-3B candidates 35 years
Budakattu (Forest Tribal) candidates residing in Karnataka forest areas 38 years

 

Category (Ex-Servicemen – Male & Female) Maximum Age
General Merit (UR) 38 years
SC / ST / Category-1 / Cat-2A / Cat-2B / Cat-3A / Cat-3B candidates 40 years

Note: Ex-servicemen must have completed 5 years of service in Karnataka Police in the PC (Civil) cadre posts (P.C.R./D.A.R./K.S.R./P.I./A.R.B./K.S.I.W./Etc.) by the last date of application and must be currently serving in those posts. They must have completed the minimum service period and must not be under any departmental inquiry/chargesheet at the time of application. Ex-servicemen from Army are entitled to 3 years of additional age relaxation for the "Avara Sevaselliside Avadhi" (period of active service). "Ex-servicemen" as defined under Army Act 1950 - Gallantry Award winners are also included.

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 – Application Fee

Fee must be paid online only. Fee once paid will NOT be refunded under any circumstances.

Category Fee
General Merit and other categories (Cat-2A / Cat-2B / Cat-3A / Cat-3B) Rs. 750/-
SC / ST / Category-1 / Ex-Servicemen / Third Gender candidates Rs. 500/-

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 – Selection Process

Selection will be through the following stages. Candidates must qualify each stage to proceed to the next. No marks are awarded for Physical Standard Test and Endurance Test - these are qualifying in nature only.

  • Stage 1 – Written Examination (Offline-OMR type): Objective type written test of 100 questions / 100 marks / 1½ hours (90 minutes). Conducted at district exam centres across the state. Candidates must mandatorily download the admit card from the authority website and carry one original identity proof to the exam centre.
  • Stage 2 – Physical Standard Test (PST) & Endurance Test (ET): Candidates who qualify the written exam at a ratio of 1:5 (per vacancy) will be called for PST and ET. Dates will be published on https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/ or https://ksp-recruitment.in/
  • Stage 3 – Medical Examination: Candidates who qualify PST and ET will be called for medical examination. Only medically fit candidates will be eligible for final appointment.
  • Stage 4 – Final Selection: Candidates who qualify all above stages will be shortlisted at a ratio of 1:2 per vacancy based on written exam marks. Final appointment is made based on merit after medical examination, as per Govt. Order dated 13.04.2026.

Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 – Exam Pattern & Syllabus

Written Examination Pattern (Offline-OMR Type):

Paper Subject Total Questions Total Marks Duration
Written Exam General Knowledge, Science, Geography, History, Indian Constitution, National Integration, Current Affairs, Mental Aptitude, and General Studies 100 100 1½ Hours (90 Minutes)

Written Exam Schedule:

Cadre Date Time
Kalyana Karnataka (371(J) – 596 Posts) 02-08-2026 2:30 PM to 4:00 PM
Mikkili / Okkalida Cadre – 3395 Posts 02-08-2026 10:30 AM to 12:00 PM
Mandatory Kannada Language Test To be notified after Written Exam result (applicable for those who have not passed Kannada at 10th/PUC level)

Candidates must score a minimum of 30 marks in the written examination as per recruitment (amendment) rules 2020 to be eligible as a competitive candidate.

Negative Marking: Each question has 4 options; only one correct answer must be marked. For every wrong answer, 0.25 marks (1/4th) will be deducted. In OMR-based answers, if 5 or more options are filled or the answer/option is struck out after the final bell and within 5 minutes, 0.25 marks will be deducted for each such question.

Physical Standard Test (PST) Standards:

Category Minimum Height Chest (For Male) Minimum Weight (For Female)

Female & Third Gender candidates 157 cm - 45 kg
Budakattu (Forest Tribal) Male candidates from Karnataka forest areas 155 cm Chest expansion of minimum 5 cm from fully expanded; overall chest not less than 75 cm -
Budakattu (Forest Tribal) Female candidates from Karnataka forest areas 150 cm - -

Endurance Test (ET) Standards:

Category Event Qualifying Standard / Distance
Male & Ex-Servicemen (Male) candidates 1600 Metre Run Within 6 minutes 30 seconds
High Jump or Long Jump (3 chances only) High Jump: Not less than 1.20 m; Long Jump: Not less than 3.80 m
Shot Put (7.26 kg) – 3 chances only Not less than 5.60 metres
   
Female, Third Gender & Ex-Servicemen (Female) candidates 400 Metre Run Within 2 minutes
High Jump or Long Jump (3 chances only) High Jump: Not less than 0.90 m; Long Jump: Not less than 2.50 m
Shot Put (4 kg) – 3 chances only Not less than 3.75 metres
   

Note: Candidates must qualify ALL events in the Endurance Test. Candidates who fail any event are disqualified from the ET. No marks are awarded for the ET; it is qualifying in nature only. Candidates are advised to practise at least one month before the ET date.

Medical Examination Standards (key disqualification criteria):

  • Vision: Distant vision: 6/9 or 6/9 (best eye) and 6/12 (other eye) without glasses; Near vision: 0/6 and 0/8. Each eye must have full field of vision. Any condition such as squint, colour blindness, or any pathological condition of the eye is disqualifying.
  • Hearing: Rinne's Test, Weber's Test, and Tests for Vertigo - any deficiency is disqualifying.
  • Varicose Veins with flatfoot: Disqualifying
  • Speech impediment: Disqualifying
  • Musculoskeletal Deformities (disqualifying): Knock Knees, Flat Foot, Bow Legs, Cubitus Valgus, Cubitus Varus, or any other defect observed during examination
  • Any physical or mental deficiency that may hinder the performance of police duties is disqualifying

How to Apply for Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026

Candidates shall apply online only through the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) portal. No other mode of application will be accepted. Only one application per post - candidates applying for both cadres must submit separate applications for each. Candidates must read all instructions before applying.

Apply Online at: https://cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea/

Documents / Details Required at the time of Application:

  • Recent passport-size photograph in JPEG format (50 KB to 200 KB)
  • Signature in black ink on white paper in JPEG format (50 KB to 70 KB)
  • Valid mobile number and e-mail ID (must remain active until recruitment process is complete)

Documents to be Produced at the time of Physical Test / Document Verification / Engagement:

  • Aadhaar Card (mandatory)
  • Marks cards and pass certificates of all subjects/semesters of the qualified post (as on last date of application)
  • Date of birth proof: SSLC / 10th standard marks card or relevant document
  • Discharge certificate and pension book / pension payment order (for Ex-Servicemen candidates)
  • Caste / Reservation certificates in prescribed Government of India formats (SC/ST: Form 'D'; Cat-1: Form 'E'; Cat-2A/2B/3A/3B: Form 'F') - must be currently valid and issued by Tahsildar or competent authority with seal, signature, and bar code/hologram
  • Rural reservation certificate (Form 1 or Form 2 as applicable) - signed by school Headmaster and Field Education Officer
  • Kannada Medium Study certificate (for KMS reservation), if applicable
  • Project Displaced Person (PDP) certificate, if applicable
  • Income and caste certificate from Tahsildar in prescribed format (for OBC categories)
  • NOC / Service certificate from employer (for candidates currently in service)
  • One original photo identity proof: Passport / Driving License / PAN Card / Service ID Card issued by State/Central Govt., PSU or Private Companies / Bank Passbook with Photo / Registered Deeds with Photo / Caste Certificate with Photo / Ex-servicemen's Pension Book / NREGS Job Card / Voter ID (EPIC) / Aadhaar Card

Training after Recruitment: Candidates appointed through direct recruitment must undergo 9 months of basic foundational training at Police Training Schools (DIGI/IGPI). Candidates who fail to qualify in the prescribed examinations during training will be dismissed from service.

Probation Period: Selected candidates will be on probation for 2 years and 6 months after appointment through direct recruitment.

For queries: Helpline – 080-23460460 (10:00 AM to 6:00 PM). Queries regarding written exam and marks only will be entertained by the Authority.

Important Instructions for Karnataka Police Constable Recruitment 2026 Candidates

  • Candidates applying online must verify all information carefully before final submission; take a printout of the application and retain the fee challan until completion of the recruitment process. No changes/modifications to the submitted application will be permitted thereafter.
  • Only Online applications are accepted; no hard copies are to be sent to the authority.
  • Candidates applying for both cadres must submit a separate application for each; apply only for one post per application.
  • OBC candidates belonging to the Creamy Layer are NOT entitled to reservation; they must apply under General Merit.
  • Caste/reservation certificates must be currently valid (not expired) as on the last date of application; certificates for SC/ST/Cat-1 may be of any validity period; for OBC categories (Cat-2A/2B/3A/3B), the certificate must be valid for 5 years. Only caste certificates obtained for employment purposes will be considered (not certificates obtained for educational or other benefits).
  • Married female candidates from OBC/other categories must produce caste certificate issued in their husband's name (not father's name) to claim reservation.
  • The Authority will not conduct any correspondence with candidates. Candidates are responsible for regularly checking the official website for updates, notifications, and corrigendum.
  • Mobile number and email provided in the application are final; no changes will be entertained subsequently.
  • Fee payment last date: If the last date falls on a public holiday, the next working day shall be the last date.
  • Candidates currently in service / having served must obtain NOC/permission from employer and submit it to the recruitment authority; service details must be mentioned in the application.
  • Any misconduct or malpractice at any stage will result in immediate disqualification from all stages of the selection process.
  • Written examination is conducted by Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA); evaluated answer sheets will be shared with Karnataka Police and the Recruitment Board for further process.
  • Canvassing in any form will result in disqualification.
  • Legal jurisdiction for any dispute arising out of this recruitment shall be Bengaluru only.
  • The authority reserves the right to cancel or modify the recruitment process at any stage without prior notice.

SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025 - Selection Process & Exam Pattern

The examination consists of two parts: Part-I (Computer Based & Written Examination, 300 marks) and Part-II (Evaluation of Record of Service/APARs, 100 marks). Total marks = 400. Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance in all parts. This is a competitive and not a qualifying examination.

Part-I: Computer Based & Written Examination (300 Marks)

Subject Paper No. No. of Questions Maximum Marks Time Duration Mode
General Awareness Paper-I 100 200 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Computer Based Examination (Objective Type Multiple Choice)
English Language and Comprehension 100
Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Paper-II -- 100 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for candidates eligible for Scribe) Written Examination (Descriptive / Conventional type)

Note: There will be negative marking of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in Computer Based Examination (Paper-I). Candidates have to attempt the examination in the language (English/Hindi) as opted in the online Application Form. There will be no Question Paper in Braille for Visually Handicapped candidates.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (100 Marks)

Marks 100 marks earmarked for evaluation of record of service (APARs - Annual Performance Assessment Reports)
Usage Marks obtained in Part-II will be added for ascertaining the rank of the candidate. Once the APARs have been evaluated, no request for change in APAR grading will be entertained by the Commission under any circumstances.

Syllabus of the Examination

Paper Subject Syllabus / Topics
Paper-I (CBE) General Awareness Questions aimed at testing General Awareness of the environment around and its application to society. Current events; matters of everyday observations and experience in their scientific aspect; History, Culture, Geography, Economics, Science, General Politics and Scientific research relating to India and neighboring countries.
Paper-I (CBE) English Language and Comprehension Understanding and knowledge of English language: Vocabulary, spelling, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, sentence completion, phrases and idiomatic use of words, comprehension of a passage. Questions will be of matriculation level.
Paper-II (Written/Descriptive) Noting, Drafting & Office Procedure Knowledge of office procedure in the Secretariat and Attached Offices; ability to write and understand notes and drafts. Candidates are required to study the Manual of Office Procedure (including Ministry of Railways version), the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Hand Book of orders issued by Ministry of Home Affairs regarding use of Hindi for official purpose of the Union, and Reservation Policy for SC/STs in services and orders issued by Government thereon from time to time.

Mode of Selection

Step 1 Based on performance in Paper-I (CBE) of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of Paper-II (Descriptive Paper) of Part-I. Candidates not qualifying Paper-I will not be evaluated for Paper-II and will not be considered for further selection.
Step 2 Based on aggregate performance in Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I, candidates will be shortlisted for evaluation of record of service (Part-II). Candidates not qualifying Part-I aggregate will not be eligible for Part-II evaluation.
Step 3 Final selection will be made on the basis of aggregate performance of candidates in Paper-I (CBE) + Paper-II (Descriptive) of Part-I and Part-II (APAR Evaluation). The Commission may fix minimum qualifying marks individually for Paper-I and Paper-II of Part-I.

Tie-Breaking Rules

1st Tie-Break Marks obtained in Paper-II (Descriptive)
2nd Tie-Break Marks obtained in part (b) of Paper-I (English Language and Comprehension)
3rd Tie-Break Date of birth - older candidates placed higher
4th Tie-Break Alphabetical order in which the names of the candidates appear

How to Apply for SSC SSA/UDC Limited Departmental Competitive Examination 2025

The Application Form must be submitted only in online mode on the SSC website https://ssc.gov.in. The process consists of two parts: (i) One Time Registration (OTR) and (ii) Filling of online Application Form for the Examination. Candidates who have not generated their OTR on the new website (https://ssc.gov.in) will be required to do so; the earlier OTR generated on the old website (https://ssc.nic.in) will not be functional for the new website.

After completion of online Application Form, the printed copy accompanied with necessary documents must be duly forwarded by the respective Service/Cadre Controlling Authority to "The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No.12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi-110003" so as to reach by 03.07.2026 (1800 hrs). Only those candidates whose application is forwarded by their Head of Department/Head of Office will be considered for admission to this Examination.

Documents to be Uploaded with Online Application:

  • Certified true copy of the first page of the Service Book duly attested by Head of Department/Head of Office (showing Name, Father's Name, Husband's Name, Nationality, SC/ST Name if applicable, Date of Birth)
  • Certified true copy of particulars of service attested by Head of Department/Head of Office (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment - substantive/officiating/permanent/temporary)
  • Copy of certificate of essential educational qualification, if applicable
  • Form of certificate for disabled Defence Personnel while in service, wherever applicable
  • Certificate of disability in case of PwBD candidates
  • Live photograph captured through the application module (plain background, no cap/mask/glasses, full frontal view)
  • Scanned signature in JPEG format (10 to 20 KB; image dimension about 6.0 cm width x 2.0 cm height)

Apply Online at: https://ssc.gov.in

Important Instructions for SSC SSA/UDC Departmental Examination 2025 Candidates

  • This is a Limited Departmental Competitive Examination - only eligible serving JSA/LDC employees of the specified 10 participating cadres can apply.
  • Only one application form should be submitted; submission of multiple applications may lead to rejection of candidature.
  • After completion of online application, the printed copy must be forwarded by the Head of Department/Office through proper channel to reach SSC (NR) by 03.07.2026 (1800 hrs); applications not forwarded through proper channel will not be considered.
  • A candidate who resigns, quits service, or whose services are terminated after applying will not be eligible for appointment on the result of this examination.
  • No change in entries made in the online application form shall be allowed at any stage under any circumstances.
  • The examination shall be conducted in Delhi NCR only; no centre will be at any Indian mission abroad. Candidates serving abroad will have to appear in India at their own expense.
  • Admission Certificate for CBE will be issued online by uploading on the website of the Northern Regional Office; it will not be issued by post. Candidates are advised to regularly visit https://sscnr.nic.in.
  • Candidates must carry their Departmental Identity Card (Original) along with hard copy of Admission Certificate for appearing in the examination.
  • Candidates who have not undergone Aadhaar Based Authentication must carry at least two passport size recent colour photographs and Original valid Photo-ID proof with Date of Birth at the examination centre.
  • There is no provision for re-evaluation/re-checking of scores of any stage/paper(s) of the Examination; no correspondence in this regard shall be entertained.
  • Tentative Answer Keys of CBE will be placed on the SSC website after the examination; candidates can submit online representations within the time limit on payment of Rs. 50/- per question (non-refundable).
  • Candidates are advised to opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during the OTR process.
  • The appearance of a candidate at the examination must match the photograph in the application form - no change in appearance is permitted.
  • All communications should be addressed to "The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, C.G.O. Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi-110003" with subject line "Senior Secretariat Assistant/Upper Division Clerk Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, 2025".
  • For Helpdesk: SSC-HQ toll-free 1800 309 3063; SSC (NR) New Delhi: 011-24363343.
  • Legal disputes, if any, shall be subject to courts/tribunals having jurisdiction over the place of the Regional Office of SSC where the candidate appeared in the examination.

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has released the notification for the Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) / Lower Division Clerk (LDC) Grade Limited Departmental Competitive Examination (LDCE), 2025 vide Notice No. 4/4/2026-CONF-5, to fill 149 vacancies across 12 Central Government departments and cadres. The online application window is open from 05th June 2026 to 26th June 2026 (up to 11:00 PM). Please note this is a limited departmental examination - only existing regular Group 'C' / Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) employees of the participating cadres are eligible, and every application must be forwarded through proper channel by the Head of Department/Office. The Computer Based Examination is tentatively scheduled for July–August 2026 and will be held in Delhi-NCR only. Check the complete eligibility, vacancy break-up, exam pattern, and step-by-step process below.

FOLLOW US

Important: Who Can Apply (and Who Cannot)

Because this is an LDCE (Limited Departmental Competitive Examination), eligibility is far narrower than an open recruitment. Read this before anything else - it is the most common point of confusion.

You CAN apply only if all of the following are true:

  • You are a regularly appointed Group 'C' employee or Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) in Level-1 / Grade Pay ₹1,800 of one of the 12 participating cadres listed below.
  • You have completed at least 3 years of regular service in that grade as on your cadre's crucial date.
  • You have passed Class 12th (Higher Secondary) or equivalent from a recognised Board.
  • Your application is forwarded by your Head of Department / Head of Office to SSC (Northern Region).

You CANNOT apply if:

  • You are a fresh candidate / general public with no qualifying government service - this exam is not open to private-sector or unemployed applicants.
  • You work in a department that is not among the 12 participating cadres.
  • Your application is not forwarded through proper channel - direct/self-submitted hard copies will be summarily rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Candidates must have passed the 12th standard (Higher Secondary) examination from a recognised Board or equivalent. For the Railway Board Secretariat Clerical Service, candidates are additionally required to pass a typing test (35 w.p.m. in English or 30 w.p.m. in Hindi on computer) within one year of appointment.

Length of Service

A minimum of three years of regular service as a Group 'C' employee / MTS in Level-1 (Grade Pay ₹1,800) in the respective cadre, counted as on the crucial date applicable to that cadre.

Crucial Date (Varies by Cadre)

The crucial date for counting approved service and age is not the same for every department. Check yours carefully:

Crucial Date Applicable Cadres

Age Limit & Relaxation

For most participating cadres, the maximum age is 45 years (50 years for SC/ST) as on the crucial date. Candidates should confirm the exact age condition for their own cadre from the notification. Permissible relaxation beyond the upper age limit:

Category Age Relaxation

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Application Fee

For this Limited Departmental Competitive Examination, the notice does not prescribe an application fee for submitting the form. (A separate, non-refundable charge of ₹50 per question applies only if a candidate later chooses to challenge the tentative answer key - this is unrelated to the application itself.)

How to Apply for SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025

The process has two parts - One Time Registration (OTR) followed by the application - plus a mandatory offline forwarding step. Follow these steps:

  1. Generate OTR on the new website. Visit ssc.gov.in and click "Register Now." Any OTR created on the old site (ssc.nic.in) will not work on the new portal.
  2. Opt for Aadhaar-Based Authentication during OTR (recommended). Candidates who skip Aadhaar must upload the prescribed proof documents.
  3. Log in with your Registration Number and password, then open the JSA/LDC LDCE 2025 link under the "Live Exam" tab and click Apply.
  4. Fill the application - service details, cadre, crucial date, length of service, and age-relaxation code (if any). Information auto-filled from OTR is non-editable; use "Modify Registration" if a correction is needed.
  5. Capture your live photograph and upload your signature as per the specifications (see below).
  6. Upload the required documents (listed below) and Submit. Take a printout of the submitted application.
  7. Forward the hard copy through proper channel. Your Head of Department / Head of Office must forward the printed application along with service documents to: The Regional Director, Staff Selection Commission (Northern Region), Block No. 12, CGO Complex, Lodhi Road, New Delhi – 110003, so as to reach by 03-07-2026 (6:00 PM) - or 10-07-2026 for candidates abroad/A&N/Lakshadweep.

Critical: Only applications forwarded by the Head of Department/Office will be admitted. A correctly submitted online form alone is not enough.

Documents to Keep Ready Before You Start

  • Certified true copy of the first page of your Service Book (attested by HoD/HoO)
  • Certified particulars of service (posts held, scale of pay, nature of appointment)
  • Class 12th certificate / educational qualification proof (if applicable)
  • Caste/Category certificate (SC/ST), if claiming reservation
  • Disability certificate (Annexure-VII / VIII) for PwBD candidates
  • A recent passport-size photo for the live capture reference, and a scanned signature

Photograph & Signature Specifications

  • Photograph: Captured live via webcam/phone, in a well-lit area with a plain background. No cap, mask, or spectacles. Face must fill the on-screen red rectangle. Pre-existing/scanned photos are rejected.
  • Signature: JPEG/JPG, 10–20 KB, dimensions about 6.0 cm × 2.0 cm. Sign so the signature fills at least 80% of the box. Blurred or miniature signatures are rejected.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Exam Pattern & Scheme

The examination carries 260 marks in total - 200 for Part-I (the exams) and 60 for Part-II (service record). Note that Paper-I is descriptive (written) and Paper-II is the objective Computer Based Test (CBT).

Part-I: Written + Computer Based Examination (200 Marks)

Paper Type Section Questions Max Marks Duration
Paper-I Descriptive (Written) Short Essay – 100 1 hr 30 min*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (a) Language - General English or Samanya Hindi 50 50 2 hrs*
Paper-II Objective (CBT) (b) General Knowledge 50 50 (combined)

*Scribe-eligible candidates get 2 hours for Paper-I and 2 hours 40 minutes for Paper-II, plus 20 minutes compensatory time per hour.

  • Negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applies to Paper-II (CBT) only. There is no negative marking in the descriptive Paper-I.
  • Candidates must attempt the exam in the language (English/Hindi) chosen in the application form.

Part-II: Evaluation of Record of Service (60 Marks)

60 marks are reserved for evaluation of the APARs (Annual Performance Appraisal Reports). These marks are added to determine the final rank. Once evaluated, no request to change APAR grading is entertained.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Selection Process

This is a competitive, not qualifying examination. Selection proceeds stage by stage:

  1. Paper-II (CBT) qualifying: Candidates must clear the minimum marks fixed for Paper-II to have their Paper-I evaluated.
  2. Paper-I (Descriptive) evaluation: Only those qualifying in Paper-II have their descriptive paper assessed.
  3. APAR evaluation (Part-II): Based on the aggregate of Paper-I + Paper-II, shortlisted candidates move to service-record evaluation.
  4. Final merit: Prepared on the combined total of Paper-I + Paper-II + Part-II (APAR) = 260 marks, cadre-wise, subject to reservation. Ties are resolved by Paper-I marks, then Paper-II part (a), then Paper-II total, then date of birth (older ranked higher), then alphabetical order.

SSC JSA / LDC LDCE 2025 - Syllabus

  • Paper-I (Short Essay): One essay of 400–500 words on any of the specified subjects.
  • Paper-II (a) Language: Simple composition and applied grammar (in the chosen English/Hindi medium).
  • Paper-II (b) General Knowledge: Current events, matters of everyday observation and experience, and general information about India.

SSC JSA / LDC Salary 2026

Selected candidates are appointed in Pay Level-2 (₹19,900 – ₹63,200 per month) under the 7th CPC, as Group 'C' Non-Gazetted staff. In addition to basic pay, employees are entitled to Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and other benefits as admissible under Central Government rules for the respective department.

Common Reasons SSC Applications Get Rejected

A large share of LDCE applications fail on avoidable mistakes. Double-check all of these before submitting:

  • Application not forwarded by the Head of Department/Office (the single biggest cause of rejection).
  • Multiple applications submitted for the same exam.
  • Photograph with a cap/spectacles, dark background, blurred, or a pre-existing (scanned) photo instead of a live capture.
  • Signature that is blurred, miniature, or below the size norm.
  • Wrong OTR details - name, father's/mother's name, or date of birth not matching the matriculation certificate (OTR data is non-editable).
  • Hard copy reaching SSC-NR after the deadline, or incomplete documents.

What to Do If the SSC Website Is Slow

Traffic on the SSC portal spikes near the closing date. If you face issues:

  • Apply during off-peak hours - late at night or early morning - rather than on the last day.
  • Clear your browser cache/cookies, or use an incognito/private tab.
  • Try a different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
  • Keep all documents pre-scanned and ready in the correct format so a session timeout doesn't cost you the whole form.
  • Save a draft frequently and take a printout immediately after final submission.

Exam Day Guidelines

  • The exam is conducted in Delhi-NCR only; there is no centre abroad. A candidate posted abroad must appear in India at their own expense.
  • The Admission Certificate is issued online via sscnr.nic.in (3–4 days before the exam); it is never sent by post.
  • Carry your original Departmental Identity Card along with a hard copy of the Admission Certificate.
  • Candidates not Aadhaar-authenticated during OTR must report early with two passport-size photographs and an original photo ID showing date of birth.
  • No Travelling Allowance is paid by SSC.
  • Mobile phones, Bluetooth/wireless devices, smartwatches, and electronic gadgets are strictly prohibited. SSC conducts post-exam log, biometric, and CCTV analysis, and malpractice attracts debarment of 1 to 7 years depending on the offence.

Helpline & Official Links

  • Help Desk (SSC-HQ): 1800-309-3063 (Toll-free)
  • SSC (Northern Region): 011-24363343
  • Official Websites: ssc.gov.in (HQ) · sscnr.nic.in (Northern Region)

DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria

Only Indian Nationals can apply. The date for determining the eligibility of all candidates in every respect shall be the prescribed Closing Date (19 June 2026). First Division means 60% marks; where CGPA/CPI of 6.75 on a 10-point scale will be taken as equivalent to 60% as per AICTE guidelines. No rounding off of marks is permitted.

Criteria Details
Essential Academic Qualification At least First Division Bachelor's Degree in Engineering/Technology in the relevant discipline OR First Division Master's Degree in the relevant discipline from a recognized University. (As detailed post-wise above)
Experience Post-qualification experience only (experience counted only after passing the essential qualification). Scientist E: 11 years; Scientist D: 7 years; Scientist C: 3 years (as on closing date). Experience below Pay Level 10 as per 7th CPC or equivalent will not be considered.
CCA Declaration / NOC All serving candidates in Government/PSU/Government-promoted companies (with 50% or more controlling stake) must upload a signed CCA Declaration at time of online submission. NOC from Cadre Controlling Authority (CCA) is mandatory at time of Final Personal Interview.
Weightage for Higher Qualification Post Graduate Qualification in Engineering: 2 years; PG Degree in Medicine/Physiology (Medical Post only): 3 years; Doctorate Degree in Science: 3 years; PhD in Pharmacy: 3 years; PhD in Engineering: 4 years. (Only if in the relevant discipline and acquired before closing date; period of study must not overlap with work experience.)
Pay Equivalence (Private Sector) Candidates from Private Sector must submit proof of Pay drawn/Cost to Company (CTC)/CTC revision document/Form 16A during the period claimed as experience. Pay drawn/CTC/Form 16A will be the sole criteria. For details visit RAC website and check 'Pay Equivalence Criteria'.

DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Screening of received applications will be carried out at multiple stages. Final selection is purely based on merit of marks scored in the Final Personal Interview.

Stage 1 – Administrative Screening: Verification of identity, age, essential & higher qualifications, length of suitable experience and CCA Declaration (wherever applicable).

Stage 2 – Technical Screening (Level-1): For all Administratively Eligible candidates - Technical Screening by holding a Meeting of Technical Screening Committee (an independent body including Technical Experts from Industry/Academia/DRDO other than RAC) using Bio-data based Technical Screening at Level-1 by: (a) Relevance of suitable experience w.r.t. advertised qualifications; (b) Relevance of Desirable/Higher Qualification; (c) Any other criteria suggested by Technical Screening Committee. Predefined Ratio for Preliminary Online Interview: Up to 24 candidates for 1 post; up to 48 candidates for 2 posts.

Stage 3 – Technical Screening (Level-2 / Preliminary Online Interview, if required): If number shortlisted for Final Personal Interview is large, further shortlisting via Preliminary Online Interview of short duration (10–15 minutes). Predefined Ratio for Final Personal Interview: Up to 12 candidates for 1 post; up to 24 candidates for 2 posts.

Stage 4 – Final Personal Interview (in-person at RAC, Delhi): Final selection is purely on merit of marks scored. Candidates must score a minimum of 75% marks (75 out of 100) in the Final Personal Interview for consideration for selection. The Final Personal Interview will be held in-person only before the Selection Board at RAC, Delhi on the scheduled date - no online/virtual interview will be considered.

Note: If administrative screening does not result in minimum 6 eligible candidates against one vacancy, the subsequent selection process for that vacancy may be cancelled. If technical screening does not result in minimum 6 candidates per vacancy for Final Personal Interview, the number of vacancies will be reduced accordingly.

Competition Level Analysis for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026

The competition level for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026 is expected to be very high, particularly for Scientist C posts in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Computer Science & Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering - disciplines with a large pool of eligible candidates and growing interest in DRDO's prestigious research environment. DRDO provides one of the best career growth structures for scientists under the Flexible Complimenting Scheme (FCS), making it a highly sought-after employer.

The multi-stage shortlisting process (Administrative → Technical Level-1 → Level-2/Preliminary Online Interview → Final Personal Interview in Delhi) is rigorous. Only up to 12 candidates per vacancy reach the Final Personal Interview, and even among those, a minimum of 75% marks in the interview is mandatory for selection. For Scientist D and E posts requiring 7–11 years of experience, the competition narrows to experienced professionals, but the specificity of required experience (e.g., Optics/Photonics, Radiation Physics, Chemical Engineering for underwater applications) naturally limits the eligible pool, making those posts relatively less competitive. Niche posts like Oceanography, Pharmacology, and Remote Sensing will see very limited candidates, improving selection chances for well-qualified applicants.

Who should NOT apply for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026?

  • Candidates who do not have First Division (60%+) in the essential qualifying degree - this is a hard minimum requirement and no rounding off is permitted.
  • Candidates with experience below Pay Level 10 (7th CPC) or equivalent - such experience will not be counted for computing the required years of experience.
  • Candidates whose period of study (higher qualification like PhD) overlaps with the work experience claimed - overlapping periods will be removed from total experience.
  • Candidates applying for Scientist D or E posts who are currently unemployed for more than one year - under current employment, the period of un-employment shall not exceed one year, else the candidature will be rejected.
  • Candidates serving in Government/PSU who do not upload a signed CCA Declaration - without CCA Declaration their candidature will be rejected, and NOC will be mandatory at Final Personal Interview.
  • Candidates from Private Sector who cannot produce CTC/Pay drawn proof/Form 16A for the claimed experience period - this is the sole criteria for establishing experience suitability from private sector.
  • Candidates exceeding the maximum age of 35 years (Scientist C), 45 years (Scientist D/E), or 56 years inclusive of all relaxations.
  • Candidates who cannot attend the Final Personal Interview in-person at RAC, Delhi - no online/virtual mode is available for Final Personal Interview under any circumstances.
  • Candidates who do not meet the specific work experience fields mentioned in the advertised qualifications - the Technical Screening Committee assesses relevance of experience very strictly.
  • Candidates applying for Scientist C (Encadered) posts from Reserved categories seeking age relaxation - there is no category-based age relaxation for Scientist C Encadered posts.

Common mistakes / What to check before applying for DRDO RAC Scientist Recruitment 2026?

  • Not checking whether your experience is at or above Pay Level 10 (7th CPC) equivalent - experience below this level is invalid and will not be counted.
  • Miscounting experience years by including the period of higher qualification (PhD/M.Tech) that overlaps with work experience - the overlapping period will be deducted.
  • Applying for multiple posts by submitting one application - candidates applying for more than one post must apply separately for each post and mention item numbers of all other posts where they have applied, along with the order of preference.
  • Not highlighting desirable qualifications and experience in the Justification column under 'Other Section' in the online application form - this is crucial for Technical Screening Committee's assessment.
  • Providing incorrect or non-verifiable experience details - the length of experience (date of joining along with Pay Scale/CTC and end date of each employment) should be available in attached experience documents.

Indian Navy Agniveer (Apprentice) Recruitment 2026 - Important Instructions

  • Only unmarried Indian male candidates are eligible. Agniveers cannot marry during their entire 4-year tenure; violation will result in dismissal from service.
  • Agniveers are enrolled under the Navy Act 1957 for a period of 4 years. Indian Navy is not obliged to retain Agniveers beyond the engagement period.
  • Up to 25% of each specific batch of Agniveers may be offered permanent enrolment in the Indian Navy as Sailors (Regular Cadre) / Artificers based on performance and organisational requirements. Selection for further enrolment is entirely at the discretion of the Indian Navy; Agniveers have no right to be selected.
  • Agniveers will not be permitted to seek release at their own request prior to completion of the engagement period.
  • Agniveers are not governed by Naval Pension Regulations/Rules and are not entitled to gratuity for the engagement period.
  • Agniveers will not be eligible for Ex-Servicemen status.
  • Candidates declaring incorrect domicile/gender and other details shall not be permitted to appear in the recruitment and their candidature will be cancelled.
  • Candidates reporting 30 minutes after the reporting time for Stage I - INET shall not be allowed to appear in the examination.
  • A candidate's selection pertaining to a particular batch is valid for that batch only. Qualified candidates whose names do not appear in the merit list cannot claim admission for the next batch.
  • Mobile phones or any other communication devices are not allowed inside the examination premises. Infringement will entail disciplinary action including ban from future examinations.
  • Candidates should not submit multiple applications. If more than one application is received, candidature will be cancelled.
  • Minimum height standard is 157 cms. Permanent body tattoos are only permitted on the inner face of forearms (inside of elbow to wrist) and on the reversed side of palm/back (dorsal) side of hand. Tattoos on any other part of the body are not acceptable.
  • Candidates are advised to get their ears cleaned for wax and tartar removed from teeth prior to medical examination.
  • Visual Standards: Uncorrected Vision 6/12, 6/12 | Corrected Vision 6/6, 6/6 | Colour Perception: CP PASS.
  • No enquiry will be entertained regarding this recruitment/enrolment after a period of six months post completion of the recruitment cycle for the respective batch.
  • The terms and conditions given in the advertisement are guidelines only and are subject to change without notice. Further, orders issued by the Government as amended from time to time will apply for selected candidates.

BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 - Selection Process

Selection will be based on Computer Based Multiple Choice Objective Type Test (CBT). All candidates will be given a score based on their performance in the CBT. A final merit list will be prepared based on total marks obtained across all three sections. Selected candidates will go for document verification and medical examination. Appearance in the final merit list does not confer any right for appointment — a final offer letter will be issued only after successful completion of all pre-appointment formalities. BSNL reserves the right to cancel/restrict/enlarge/modify/alter the recruitment/selection process at any stage without notice.

Section Name of Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration

Marking Scheme: For each correct answer: +4 Marks. For each wrong answer: -1 Mark (Negative Marking). The standard of engineering papers will be that of Engineering Degree Examination of an Indian University. In the General Ability Test, special attention will be paid to assess the candidate's capacity for general awareness, at the level expected of an Engineering Graduate. If the examination is held in multiple sessions, normalization of marks will be adopted. Minimum Qualifying Marks: For UR/OBC (CL) candidates — minimum 40% in each section and minimum 50% overall across all three sections combined. For SC/ST/OBC (NCL)/PwBD/EWS candidates — minimum 35% in each section and minimum 45% overall. Candidates not meeting sectional or overall minimum qualifying marks will not be included in the merit list. The final merit list will be prepared based on total marks in all three sections combined, subject to minimum qualifying marks criteria being met.

Stage 2 – Document Verification

Candidates in the declared merit list will be called for document verification. Date and venue will be intimated in due course. All original certificates along with self-attested photocopies must be produced at the time of document verification.

Stage 3 – Medical Examination

Appointment of selected candidates will be subject to their passing the Company's Medical Examination as per standards laid down by BSNL. Candidates who are already employed elsewhere must resign from their current organization only after being declared medically fit. Details will be provided on BSNL website www.bsnl.co.in.

BSNL JTO Direct Recruitment 2026 - Exam Pattern & Syllabus

The examination is a Computer Based Multiple Choice Objective Type Test (CBT) of 3 hours duration consisting of three sections. Sections I and II cover Engineering Stream subjects at B.E./B.Tech. degree level, and Section III covers General Ability. The detailed syllabus topic-wise is given below.

Section I – Engineering Stream (Topics)

Topic Key Subtopics
1. Materials and Components Structure and properties of Electronic Engineering materials; Conductors, Semiconductors and Insulators; Magnetic, Ferroelectric, Piezoelectric, Ceramic, Optical and Superconducting materials; Passive components and characteristics – Resistors, Capacitors, Inductors; Ferrites, Quartz crystal, Ceramic resonators; Electromagnetic and Electromechanical components.
2. Physical Electronics, Electron Devices and ICs Electrons and holes in semiconductors; Carrier Statistics; Mechanics of current flow in a semi-conductor; Hall effect; Junction theory; Different types of diodes and their characteristics; Bipolar Junction transistor; Field effect transistors; Power switching devices like SCRs, CTOs, power MOSFETs; Basics of ICs-bipolar, MOS and CMOS types; Basics of Opto Electronics.
3. Network Theory Network analysis techniques; Network theorem; Transient and steady state sinusoidal response; Transmission criteria – delay and rise time, Elmore's and other definitions; Effect of cascading; Elements of network synthesis.
4. Electromagnetic Theory Transmission lines – basic theory, standing waves, matching applications, microstrip lines; Basics of waveguides and resonators; Elements of antenna theory.
5. Electronic Measurements and Instrumentation Basic concepts, standards and error analysis; Measurements of basic electrical quantities and parameters; Electronic measuring instruments and their principles of working – analog and digital, comparison, characteristics, applications; Transducers; Electronic measurements of non-electrical quantities like temperature, pressure, humidity; Basics of telemetry for industrial use.
6. Power Electronics Power Semiconductor devices; Thyristor; Power transistor; MOSFETs; Characteristics and operation; AC to DC convertors; 1-Phase and 3-phase DC to DC Convertors; AC regulators; Thyristor controlled reactors; Switched capacitor networks; Inverters – Single-phase and 3-phase; Pulse width modulation; Sinusoidal modulation with uniform sampling; Switched mode power supplies.

Section II – Engineering Stream (Topics)

Topic Key Subtopics
1. Analog Electronic Circuits Transistor biasing and stabilization; Small Signal analysis; Power amplifiers; Frequency response; Wide band techniques; Feedback amplifiers; Tuned amplifiers; Oscillators; Rectifiers and power supplies; Operational Amplifier; Other linear integrated circuits and applications; Pulse shaping circuits and waveform generators.
2. Digital Electronic Circuits Transistor as a switching element; Boolean algebra; Simplification of Boolean functions; Karnaugh Map and applications; IC Logic gates and their characteristics; IC logic families – DTL, TTL, ECL, NMOS, PMOS and CMOS gates and their comparison; Combinational logic circuits; Half adder, full adder; Digital Compartor; Multiplexer; Demultiplexer; ROM and their applications; Flip-flops – R-S, J-K, D and T types; Different types of counters and registers; Waveform generators; A/D and D/A converters; Semiconductor memories.
3. Control Systems Transient and steady state response of control systems; Effect of feedback on stability and sensitivity; Root locus techniques; Frequency response analysis; Concepts of gain and phase margins; Constant-M and Constant-N Nichol's Chart; Approximation of transient response from Constant-N Nichol's Chart; Approximation of transient response from closed loop frequency response; Design of Control Systems; Compensators; Industrial controllers.
4. Communication Systems Basic information theory; Modulation and detection in analogue and digital systems; Sampling and data reconstruction; Quantization & Coding; Time division and frequency division multiplexing; Equalisation; Optical Communication – in free space & fibre optic; Propagation of signals at HF, VHF, UHF and microwave frequency; Satellite communication.
5. Microwave Engineering Microwave Tubes and solid state devices; Microwave generation and amplifiers; Waveguides and other Microwave Components and Circuits; Microstrip circuits; Microwave antennas; Microwave Measurements; MASERS; LASERS; Microwave Propagation; Microwave Communication Systems – terrestrial and satellite based.
6. Computer Engineering Number Systems; Data representation; Programming; Elements of a high level programming language PASCAL/C; Use of basic data structures; Fundamentals of computer architecture processor design; Control unit design; Memory organization; I/O System Organization; Personal computers and their typical uses.
7. Microprocessors Microprocessor architecture – Instruction set and simple assembly language programming; Interfacing for memory and I/O; Applications of Microprocessors in Telecommunications and power system.

Section III – General Ability Test

Topic Key Subtopics
General Ability Test General English comprehension and understanding; Current Events and General Knowledge; Everyday observation and experience in scientific aspects as may be expected of an educated person; Events and developments in Telecommunications; History of India; Geography. Questions will be of a nature that can be answered without special study by an educated person.

The examination will be held in 27 cities/centres across India. Candidates must choose only one Examination City/Centre at the time of registration. The exam centre may be any of the 27 cities or a nearby city depending upon number of candidates.
